title: [C13T3] Top ten countries for the production and consumption of electricity in 2014
prompt: The bar chart below shows the top ten countries for the production and consumption of electricity in 2014. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares electricity production and consumption figures for the top ten countries in 2014.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, China and the United States were by far the largest producers and consumers of electricity, with China leading by a significant margin. Most countries produced more electricity than they consumed, with Germany being a notable exception.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the top producers, China generated 5,398 billion kWh of electricity, marginally more than its consumption of 5,322 billion kWh. The United States ranked second, producing 4,099 billion kWh and consuming 3,866 billion kWh. Russia came in third place with a production and consumption of 1,057 billion kWh, followed by Japan at 936.2 billion kWh, and India with 871 billion kWh.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Among the remaining countries, Canada, France, and Brazil each produced between 500 and 620 billion kWh, with their consumption levels consistently lower than production, ranging from 455 billion to 500 billion kWh. Germany was unique among the top ten, consuming more electricity (582.5 billion kWh) than it produced (526.6 billion kWh). Korea, ranking tenth, had the lowest figures in both categories, producing 485.1 billion kWh and consuming 449.5 billion kWh.
